root_cause.text: The `sev_ioctl_do_pdh_export` function fails to check the return status of the PSP firmware command (`SEV_CMD_PDH_CERT_EXPORT`) before copying certificate blobs to userspace, allowing a command failure (e.g., due to an invalid length) to trigger an out-of-bounds read when `copy_to_user` uses the firmware-updated length that exceeds the allocated kernel buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a guard `if (ret || WARN_ON_ONCE(argp->error)) goto e_free_cert;` immediately after the command execution and before copying data to userspace. The CVE description explicitly states: "When retrieving the PDH cert, don't attempt to copy the blobs to userspace if the firmware command failed. If the failure was due to an invalid length, i.e. the userspace buffer+length was too small, copying the number of bytes _firmware_ requires will overflow the kernel-allocated buffer and leak data to userspace." The KASAN report confirms a slab-out-of-bounds read during `copy_to_user` in the same function.

intent_record.what: Replaced a single-line comment with a multi-line comment describing the firmware's behavior regarding blob lengths.
intent_record.how: No runtime behavior change; the comment now explains that firmware returns either the minimum required length or the actual length written, which clarifies the purpose of the length assignments.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add missing error check for ret and argp->error to abort and cleanup on failure.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check for 'ret' or 'argp->error' after a previous operation in sev_ioctl_do_pdh_export, causing a jump to the error cleanup label 'e_free_cert' if either is true.
intent_record.how: This prevents the function from proceeding to copy data to user space or releasing resources when an error has occurred, ensuring proper cleanup and avoiding potential use of invalid data.
